content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop too sharply, missing sustained upward momentum.
- Model underestimates late-period price increases, particularly after 25–30 days of history.
- Overshoots occur after sharp upward moves in history; model reacts too aggressively to recent spikes.
- Mean reversion bias: model assumes prices return to prior averages too quickly, ignoring structural trends.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in capturing true price momentum; model is too slow to react to new data.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of price increases after 80–85 range; tends to cap forecasts at 85–88.
- Forecasts are too optimistic in the first 10–15 days of the 30d window, then gradually adjust downward.
